name: Slack
summary: Self-serve and no review is required. A new Slack app installs only in the workspace where you created it, so you must turn on public distribution (instant, takes a checklist) before customers can connect. A Marketplace listing is optional and reviewed. You need HTTPS everywhere and correct bot vs user scopes.

verdict.label: Easy
verdict.timeToProduction: Same day, after you activate public distribution
verdict.approvalWait: None for public distribution. The Slack Marketplace listing is a separate review with extra prerequisites.
verdict.handsOnEffort: 1–2 hours, including HTTPS redirect setup and testing in a second workspace

decideFirst.question: Bot token, user token, or both?
decideFirst.guidance: Bot scopes give a bot token (xoxb-) that acts as your app. User scopes give a user token (xoxp-) that acts as the installing user. An agent that reads a user's DMs or searches as them needs user scopes. Configure the scope list that matches what your authorize URL requests.

decideFirst.question: Unlisted public distribution, or a Marketplace listing?
decideFirst.guidance: Public distribution lets any workspace install your app through your own install link, with no review. Some workspaces only allow Marketplace-listed apps, or only let admins install apps. That is when a listing matters.

steps.title: Create an app at api.slack.com/apps
steps.detail: Start from a manifest. The agent can write the manifest YAML with your scopes and redirect URLs.

steps.title: Add redirect URLs under OAuth & Permissions
steps.detail: Must be HTTPS and can't contain an anchor (#). Slack doesn't accept http://, even for localhost. Use a tunnel for local testing.

evidence.note: The 'not even localhost' detail comes from a secondary source

steps.title: Add bot and/or user scopes
steps.detail: You can't remove scopes from an existing token without revoking it, so start small.

steps.title: Copy client ID, client secret, and signing secret
steps.detail: These are under Basic Information → App Credentials.

steps.title: Redirect to slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize, then call oauth.v2.access
steps.detail: If you register several redirect URLs, send the same redirect_uri in both steps or the exchange fails. The agent can write and test this.

steps.title: Manage Distribution → complete checklist → Activate Public Distribution
steps.detail: Every URL must use SSL. Remove hard-coded tokens. Slack's docs say activation needs no review.

steps.title: Test from a different workspace
steps.detail: Use an incognito window and a workspace that isn't your dev workspace.

steps.title: (Optional) Submit to the Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Reviewed listing. One integration platform reports these prerequisites: 5+ active workspace installs and a security review of your endpoints.

evidence.note: Thresholds not checked against Slack's own Marketplace guidelines

requirements.item: SSL on all app URLs + no hard-coded tokens

blockers.cause: Someone outside your dev workspace tried to install before distribution was on
blockers.fix: Activate Public Distribution. You don't need a Marketplace listing.

blockers.cause: The redirect_uri doesn't match, isn't below a registered URL, or differs between authorize and exchange
blockers.fix: Send an identical redirect_uri in both calls and register the exact base URL.

blockers.symptom: Install blocked in a customer workspace
blockers.cause: The workspace requires admin approval or allows only Marketplace apps
blockers.fix: Ask their admin to approve the app, or pursue a Marketplace listing.

nuances.title: Token rotation is opt-in and hard to undo
nuances.detail: With rotation on, access tokens expire after 12 hours and must be refreshed. Treat turning it on as one-way.

nuances.title: PKCE apps always get expiring refresh tokens
nuances.detail: Per a March 2026 changelog: installs that redirect to a custom URI scheme always get rotating tokens, and PKCE-enabled refresh tokens expire after 30 days.

nuances.title: Turning distribution off uninstalls your app
nuances.detail: Deactivating public distribution removes the app from every workspace except the original. Once you are listed in the Marketplace, you can't deactivate this way.

checked: HTTPS and no-anchor redirect rules, and the same-redirect_uri-in-both-steps rule, against Slack's 'Installing with OAuth' page
Distribution checklist, workspace install restrictions, and deactivation behavior against Slack's distribution page
corrected: Older guides link to api.slack.com docs. Slack's docs now live at docs.slack.dev, so we cite the new location.
unverified: Marketplace listing prerequisites (5 active workspaces, security review) come from one secondary source.
The 12-hour rotating token lifetime comes from a secondary source.
